heading: HOW CONSUMER DESIRE FOR MORE TACTILE, IRL EXPERIENCES CONTINUES TO TRANSFORM MARKETING (20 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Gen Z is seeking offline experiences as digital fatigue grows, with 82% saying social media breaks improve their mental health and 70% planning to take up hands-on hobbies. Across the US, 75% see a simpler relationship with technology as a lifestyle upgrade. 68% collect physical items and 84% of Gen Z go out of their way for in-person shopping.

heading: HALF OF MARKETING TEAMS ARE REPLACING PEOPLE WITH AI. ALMOST NOBODY CAN PROVE IT'S WORKING (4 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Nearly 48% of marketing teams replaced human tasks with AI in the past year, but few can prove it works. A Basis survey found 65% of respondents either don't measure AI's return on investment or don't know if their organization does. Meanwhile, 51% expect substantial job losses across the industry within 3-5 years, even as AI's impact on marketing performance remains largely unproven.

heading: DOES AI DRIVE MORE DIRECT TRAFFIC? (6 MINUTE READ)
blurb: An analysis of 12 GA4 properties found no reliable evidence that AI-driven visits are hiding in Direct traffic. Total Direct sessions rose 141% from January to September, but engaged sessions stayed nearly flat due to bot traffic. Across 632 tests, AI visibility also showed no consistent link to subsequent branded search or Direct traffic. To measure AI's impact, track brand mentions across consistent prompts and platforms. Ask leads how they discovered you, then connect their responses to qualified leads, purchases, and revenue.

heading: HOW A24 MADE ‘YOU CAN SEE EVERYTHING' A MUST-SEE FILM (7 MINUTE READ)
blurb: A24 had just 40 days to market its Elizabeth Holmes documentary, despite audiences already knowing the Theranos story from TV dramas and years of trial coverage. The campaign used cryptic teasers and provocative posters to make this version feel fresh. It built intrigue without spoiling the film's biggest surprises or making Holmes look like she was staging a comeback.

heading: ARE YOU TRACKING THE RIGHT PROMPTS? (WEBINAR)
blurb: Searchable is hosting a 60-minute working session on AI visibility tracking. They'll walk through how to map what buyers ask AI about your category, check where competitors win, and build your list of what to track next. The free webinar will take place today at 11 AM ET.

heading: JOURNOFINDER (TOOL)
blurb: Journofinder builds targeted media lists and secure press coverage. Its AI agent finds journalists with verified contact details, while its article search and real-time news alerts help PR teams identify timely pitching opportunities. It integrates with ChatGPT and Claude to streamline PR workflows.

heading: GOOGLE ADS NOW IN AI MODE WITH PERSONAL INTELLIGENCE (2 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Google is testing ads in AI Mode for users who enable Personal Intelligence by connecting apps like Gmail and Google Photos. While ads won't be based directly on inboxes or photo libraries, Google may use summaries and inferences from connected apps to personalize ad targeting. Advertisers won't have access to users' connected apps, and sensitive information won't be used to tailor ads.

heading: CHATGPT, CLAUDE, AND GROK CHATS REACH TRACKERS, STUDY FINDS (3 MINUTE READ)
blurb: A study of 17 AI assistant experiences found that 8 shared conversation links, titles, or text with advertising and analytics firms. ChatGPT, Claude, and Grok all leaked shared chat links, while Grok also sent screenshots and prompts to Google, Meta, and TikTok. Rejecting cookies left 80.8% of trackers active, and 6 of 9 web assistants still contacted Google Ads. The findings highlight privacy risks for users discussing sensitive topics, even when AI providers offer training opt-outs.

heading: CUSTOMER-CENTRIC THINKING IS TOO NARROW (9 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Customer-centric marketing can overlook people who never buy but still influence how a market discovers and evaluates a brand. Journalists and practitioners shape public conversations and the information that search engines and AI systems use. Audience-centric marketing considers these groups when creating content and prioritizes resources that are easy to access, cite, and share. This can make ungated research and public documentation more valuable than lead-generation metrics suggest.

heading: MORE THAN HALF OF PODCAST LISTENERS SAY AD LOAD IS TOO HIGH (3 MINUTE READ)
blurb: 55% of podcast listeners say there are too many ads, while host-read spots outperform prerecorded ads.

heading: CAN SOCIAL MEDIA BANS PROTECT YOUNG PEOPLE'S MENTAL HEALTH? (5 MINUTE READ)
blurb: In Australia, 61% of children ages 12-15 still access banned platforms using false IDs or VPNs.

heading: ‘NO INFLUENCERS': THE HOTELS, RESTAURANTS AND BEAUTY SPOTS RESTRICTING PHOTOSHOOTS (4 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Hotels and restaurants are restricting photography as visitors use them as content backdrops rather than places to eat or stay.

heading: CONSUMERS RETHINK VALUE AS UNCERTAINTY AND INFLATION PERSIST (2 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Consumers are adopting 3 distinct spending behaviors depending on the purchase. Some pay more for premium experiences and better performance. Others balance quality and convenience against price to get the most from every dollar. Those seeking to limit spending choose cheaper alternatives and promotions while protecting budgets for priorities. These behaviors aren't fixed consumer segments. The same person may splurge in one category while trading down in another depending on the occasion and perceived value.

heading: GOOGLE IS FEEDING RANK TRACKERS POISONED SERPS WITH SWAPPED RESULTS, NOZZLE FINDS (3 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Google has been feeding rank trackers fake search results since September 13. Nozzle found that 8.4% of SERPs were affected across 27M results analyzed. The poisoned pages look normal but retain just 22% of their usual sites. This causes tracked top-10 rankings to disappear 60.2% of the time. Social platforms and forums appear more often in these results. SEO teams should cross-check ranking drops against Google Search Console before assuming their rankings have changed.

heading: PR FOR GEO: 4 WAYS IT CAN INFLUENCE AI VISIBILITY (11 MINUTE READ)
blurb: PR can improve AI visibility by earning citations for original research, reinforcing how third-party publications describe a brand, building backlinks, and increasing brand awareness. Research tied to customer pain points is more likely to earn useful AI citations than data that is merely related to the business. Consistently using the same brand descriptor in pitches and press releases can also help AI associate a company with its intended category. Measure one specific goal by establishing a baseline and tracking the same prompts across AI platforms over time. Media placements alone do not prove an impact on AI visibility, so report coverage separately from changes in citations, mentions, and recommendations.

heading: META PERFORMANCE UNLOCKED: VIRTUAL EDITION (WEBINAR)
blurb: Meta is bringing performance marketers, growth leaders, and agency partners together for one focused hour on the strategies that drive results during the holiday season. They'll cover seasonal trends, signal optimization, creative diversification, and more. The free webinar will take place on October 22 at 12:30 PM ET.

heading: SPOTIFY LAUNCHES PAID PODCAST MEMBERSHIPS WITH PERKS BEYOND BONUS CONTENT (2 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Spotify is giving podcasters a subscription revenue stream that doesn't depend on ads as it pushes deeper into video podcasts to compete with YouTube. Creators keep 90% of membership revenue and can mix perks like fewer ads, early access, and bonus video across multiple tiers.

heading: THE DISABILITY INCLUSION EFFECT (3 MINUTE READ)
blurb: In tests with more than 4,500 participants, Ads featuring a model with a disability made people 33% more likely to choose the product. The lift holds even when people are told the brand cast a wheelchair user only to meet regulations. However, it disappears when the ad calls attention to the disability or portrays the person as vulnerable, since the benefit comes from treating a stigmatized group as ordinary customers.

heading: I ANALYZED 1,100+ MARKETING JOB POSTS. THEY'RE STUCK IN 2023 (26 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Companies are treating AI system-building as one specialist's job rather than a baseline requirement for every marketing hire. Every GTM engineer post asks for AI skills, compared with 47% of marketing posts overall and just 25% of entry-level ones. Only 6% ask candidates to contribute to the shared skills, context, and agents a team runs on, and only 8% ask for proof of AI use.

heading: PINTEREST'S HOLIDAY BRAND GUIDE (3 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Pinterest users saved 63M festive ideas, while 64% say it boosts shopping confidence and 36% of ad impact comes after 8 weeks.

heading: META MUSE EXPOSES USERS' PERSONAL AND BUSINESS SECRETS WHEN THEY SHARE CONVERSATIONS (3 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Muse puts each conversation's title in its share link's web address, so passive DNS records make those links searchable by anyone.

blurb: TLDR MARKETING 2026-10-22

heading: TRY IT →
CREATORS NOW RIVAL SEARCH FOR GEN Z PRODUCT DISCOVERY (3 MINUTE READ)
blurb: 33% of Gen Z now discover products through creator posts, 4 points behind online search, and 67% bought something in the past year because an influencer endorsed it. Small creators convert as often as famous ones, since buyers weigh honesty and actual product use well above popularity. Trust in influencers among Gen Z and millennials has risen 13 points since 2019 as trust in friends and family fell, cutting the gap between them from 33 points to 15.

heading: SHOPPING HABITS BY GENERATION: WHAT BRANDS NEED TO KNOW (7 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Shopping habits vary by generation, shaping where consumers discover products and how they buy. 66% of shoppers purchased products discovered on social media, rising to 79% for Gen Z and 76% for Millennials. Younger shoppers respond to creator content and AI recommendations, while Boomers favor trusted retailers and in-store shopping.

heading: WE BOUGHT A BRAND NEW DOMAIN. 4 MONTHS LATER IT HAD $22K IN REVENUE (5 MINUTE READ)
blurb: A new domain reached 134 domain authority in under 4 months by joining a network of established businesses that regularly linked to each other through relevant blog posts. Rather than buying cheap backlinks or publishing content alone, the team secured links from 51 trusted websites and created posts targeting buyer questions and competitor pages cited by AI. The site began winning 20 keywords weekly across Google and AI search and generated $22,478 from 14 paying customers.

heading: HANDS ON: DIY GUIDE TO ANIMATED LINKEDIN INFOGRAPHICS (3 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Tim Scheuer's process for creating animated B2B LinkedIn infographics starts with writing an original insight, designing a static graphic, then animating it in Claude Code using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. He builds a reusable project repository containing brand guidelines, fonts, icons, coded components, audience profiles, and past posts to keep the output consistent with his voice. Claude generates and reviews the animation through multiple rounds before Scheuer approves the final version. He batches five posts on Sundays, repurposes ideas across LinkedIn, X, and his newsletter, then uses engagement data to identify qualified prospects and start conversations.

heading: HOW TO PRINT PIPELINE WITH B2B ADS (LIVE SERIES)
blurb: Addie's “How to Print Pipeline With B2B Ads” is a 7-session live series covering B2B advertising. Experts share tactics and offer live teardowns of attendee ads and landing pages. The next session is Thursday, October 22, when Dylan Hey will cover creating scroll-stopping B2B ads through stronger concepts and testing.

heading: GEO IS A DISTRACTION (6 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Optimizing for ChatGPT citations and other LLM mentions is a distraction because AI tools generated just 0.73% of Google Organic's traffic across 100 websites, while Google Organic accounted for 96.5% of tracked conversions. Focus on conversions and user satisfaction across Google Search, including AI Overviews and AI Mode, rather than chasing AI visibility metrics. Longer term, there are opportunities in agentic commerce through Google Merchant Center and Universal Cart, the Universal Commerce Protocol for agent-led purchases, WebMCP tools that let AI agents use website functions, and smart eyewear that enables new shopping and service interactions. You can begin preparing by improving product data and experimenting with agent accessible tools as these technologies develop.

heading: YOUR NEWSLETTER HAS TWO READERS NOW (5 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Your newsletter now has two readers: the human subscriber and the AI that may summarize, prioritize, or retrieve your email on the subscriber's behalf. AI summaries in Apple Mail, Outlook, and Yahoo can replace your preview text or condense your content, potentially changing what readers notice and whether they click. A Twilio and Inbox Monster test found that subject lines and live text near the top of an email helped shape Apple's summaries, while images and alt text provided less useful information. Test how your newsletter appears in these inboxes, make your main stories and sponsor messages clear in live text, and measure engagement through multiple signals rather than relying on open rates alone.

heading: COMMISSION ISN'T ENOUGH: 57 CREATORS SAY THEY WANT MORE FROM AFFILIATE PROGRAMS (4 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Affiliate programs are more effective when brands treat creators as long-term partners rather than relying on commissions alone. Although 68% of surveyed creators still accept affiliate commissions, many say the rates don't justify the work without additional payment, product gifting, and brand support. 72% of creators said brands don't provide new products often enough, and most prefer monthly gifting. Creators also want more hands-on management, including regular communication, performance reviews, and promotional resources. Tiered commissions, bonuses, and ongoing relationship management can help brands keep affiliates active and build sustained revenue.

heading: CHATGPT HAS PLENTY OF ADVERTISERS, BUT NOT MUCH REVENUE (4 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Cheap clicks and self-serve buying have drawn experiments rather than sustained budgets.

heading: DISNEY AND NETFLIX ARE COURTING CREATORS. YOUTUBE IS PLAYING HARDBALL TO KEEP THEM (6 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Netflix, Disney, and Tubi are investing in creator and podcast programming, while YouTube has responded with more brand-deal resources.
